title: fix(matrix): keep attachment filenames out of agent body text
body:
Closes #165416

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix attachments without captions were forwarded to the agent with their default filename as user-authored body text even after media resolution succeeded.

## User Impact

Recognized media with an explicit filename equal to its body now uses the resolved attachment placeholder. Genuine differing captions, including filename-looking captions, retain their original text. Missing/blank filenames and non-media messages keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The successful-media branch bypassed the existing Matrix attachment classifier. This reuses that owner for explicit filename metadata rather than guessing from extensions. Downloads, transport, authorization, failed-download markers, pending group history, and the separate audio-preflight heuristic are unchanged.

Thanks to @ooiuuii for the report and fix. The contributor's commit is unchanged. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes in the two changed files.

## Evidence

Verified on candidate **59979f5a511b27036ac66a8d5e886790c1f1507b**, using a built Gateway, its built Matrix plugin, and a real local Synapse homeserver on an internal Docker network with no external access. Registered separate bot/sender accounts, created rooms through the Matrix client API, uploaded a real PNG through the media API, and sent `m.room.message` events through the client API. The Gateway performed its normal Matrix sync, media download, ingress handling, and model dispatch. A scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint recorded the actual model requests and returned replies delivered back to Matrix.

Crabline 0.1.28 was checked first: its Matrix mock returns `404 M_UNRECOGNIZED` for media download routes. The real local homeserver was used instead; neither media resolution nor the handler was mocked.

Baseline: candidate runtime with the **only production change** reverted to the exact parent **bbaabd6ced15ea00fd7c7ffc82c115b30a727927**, rebuilding the Matrix plugin before starting a separate baseline Gateway/profile. The original helper is also byte-identical on main **10080eaf91bc314a6703c8edd629f499c0a0190b** (SHA-256 `f15eb1142d6aba4e8fe24602f5f6d2bbaf9b5dd9d022f4175d48e6084256318b`). This was not a claim of running the entire newer main checkout.

The triggering event was:

```json
{"msgtype":"m.image","body":"IMG_1234.png","filename":"IMG_1234.png","url":"mxc://matrix.test/<uploaded-media-id>","info":{"mimetype":"image/png","size":68,"w":1,"h":1}}
```

Observed final user-text line in the **actual model request**, after the attachment metadata:

| Matrix event | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Body and filename both `IMG_1234.png` | `IMG_1234.png` | `[matrix media]` |
| Differing caption `A real caption` | `A real caption` | `A real caption` |
| Filename-looking differing caption `other-file.png` | `other-file.png` | `other-file.png` |
| Body `IMG_1234.png`, no filename field | `IMG_1234.png` | `IMG_1234.png` |
| Plain `m.text` | `Plain text unchanged` | `Plain text unchanged` |

Every image case on both baseline and candidate included the uploaded image's exact `data:image/png;base64,...` bytes in the model request, alongside the staged inbound attachment metadata. Thus the filename-to-placeholder result occurs after successful real media resolution, not a failed download or a pre-resolved helper fixture. Filename information remains in attachment metadata; it no longer appears as authored body text in the captionless case.

## Focused Native Regression

Ran the committed regression file unchanged in Node **24.21.0**, Linux arm64, in secretless Docker:

```text
pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler-helpers.inbound-body.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

Baseline: 5 failed / 8 passed; wall 18.904 s
Candidate: 13 passed; wall 24.324 s
Candidate Vitest duration: 22.48 s (93% transform)
```

The five baseline failures are the explicit audio/file/image/video filenames and the suffixless filename. The controls pass on both. An initial invocation overlapped the build and was rejected by the compiler-input guard before tests ran; the timing above is the subsequent completed native run after the build finished.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37278092339) is green, including native regression, production/test type checks and lint. The hosted three-file/18-test shard took **44.83 s**, distinct from the isolated local file's wall time above.

## Live Provider Gate

The restored exact candidate Gateway also completed one real **gpt-5-mini** call through its HTTP chat-completions endpoint: **reasoning `low`, output budget 4096**, upstream HTTP **200**, Gateway HTTP **200**, answer **`LIVE_GATE_OK`**. A one-call credential-isolated proxy recorded only the model/effort/budget/status; the real API key never entered source, logs, or retained evidence and was deleted after the run. An initial custom-endpoint fixture omitted reasoning compatibility, so the proxy rejected it locally before any external call; adding the endpoint's explicit reasoning compatibility produced the single real call above.
